title: Bounded complexes belong to triangulated subcategories containing their terms
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] whose unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ exists [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal S$ be a strictly full triangulated subcategory of $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]: it contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, all integer shifts, and taking the third vertex of a distinguished triangle when the other two vertices belong to it. Let $C^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of objects of $\mathcal A$, and let $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $C^q=0$ whenever $q<a$ or $q>b$. If $C^q[0]\in\mathcal S$ for every $a\leq q\leq b$, then the image of $C^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ belongs to $\mathcal S$. Here $C^q[0]$ denotes the single complex with term $C^q$ in degree zero. No retract closure, flatness, projectivity, or condition on the cohomology objects is assumed; the conclusion includes an empty support interval.

source.place: Tag 0FCP, lemma-K-bounded-derived, proof: the displayed stupid-truncation triangles and finite induction, extracted as a sublemma (not the K-group assertion).

proof.text: Fix the upper bound b. Induct on a natural number n, proving the claim for every complex L supported in [c,b] with b+1-c <= n, with its degree-zero single terms in S on that interval. Taking n=(b+1-a).toNat proves the desired case. If n=0, or if c>b at any induction step, every term of L is zero by the support condition, so the identity of L is zero degreewise. Thus L is a zero object, Q(L) is a zero object, and S contains it.

source.place: Tag 0FCP, lemma-K-bounded-derived, proof: displayed stupid-truncation triangles and finite induction (lines 9112–9128).

proof.text: When c<=b, construct p:L -> single_c(L^c) with identity component in degree c and zero components elsewhere, using HomologicalComplex.mkHomToSingle. The only condition for this to be a chain map is that the differential entering degree c is zero; its source L^(c-1) is zero by the lower support bound. The component p^c is an isomorphism, and every other component has zero target, so p is degreewise epi and hence epi as a morphism of complexes.

source.place: Tag 0FCP, lemma-K-bounded-derived, proof: displayed stupid-truncation triangles and finite induction (lines 9112–9128).

proof.text: Let T be the categorical kernel of p, a concrete limit determined up to unique compatible isomorphism. The sequence 0 -> T -> L -> single_c(L^c) -> 0 is short exact. Evaluation in each degree preserves its short exactness. In degree c the last arrow is an isomorphism, so T^c is zero. In every degree q different from c, its last object is zero, so T^q -> L^q is an isomorphism. Therefore T is supported in [c+1,b], and its degree-zero single terms on that interval belong to S by transport from those of L. This kernel realizes the next stupid tail, without any arbitrary choice of data from an existence theorem.

source.place: Tag 0FCP, lemma-K-bounded-derived, proof: displayed stupid-truncation triangles and finite induction (lines 9112–9128).

proof.text: The integer-shift isomorphism of DerivedCategory.singleFunctors identifies single_c(L^c) with the shift by -c of single_0(L^c). The term hypothesis at c, integer-shift closure and isomorphism closure therefore put Q(single_c(L^c)) in S.

source.place: Tag 0FCP, lemma-K-bounded-derived, proof: displayed stupid-truncation triangles and finite induction (lines 9112–9128).

proof.text: In the successor case n+1, the bound b+1-c <= n+1 implies b+1-(c+1) <= n. The induction hypothesis applies to T using Step 3. Apply lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle to the short exact sequence of Step 3 to obtain a distinguished triangle Q(T) -> Q(L) -> Q(single_c(L^c)) -> Q(T)[1]. Its first vertex belongs to S by induction and its third by Step 4. The middle-vertex closure of a strictly full triangulated subcategory, supplied by ObjectProperty.ext_of_isTriangulatedClosed₂ (equivalently the rotation argument of the source), gives S(Q(L)).

lean.statement: theorem bounded_complex_mem_triangulated {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] (S : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory C)) [S.IsTriangulated] [S.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (a b : ℤ) (hK : ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero (K.X q)) (hS : ∀ q : ℤ, a ≤ q → q ≤ b → S ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor C 0).obj (K.X q))) : S (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)
